fragments.text: Amara
Tomasz
Priya
Kenji
Lucía
Samir
Grace
Oluwaseun
Pasted in an essay and asked if it was good. Meant: is it good enough, and am I.
Asked for the causes of the First World War, then, an hour later, whether it's normal to be this tired.
Has been chasing the same error since lunch. It was a typo in the end. Said thank you twice.
Wanted a regular expression, and then, reading it, wanted to understand it too.
On a break at three in the morning, asking how to explain a result to a frightened family in plain words.
Wants a bedtime story about a dragon who's afraid of the dark, with the child's name in it.
Trying to remember how to divide fractions before their daughter asks again.
Writing a sign about new opening hours. Wants it to sound friendly, not sorry.
Learning to video-call a grandson. Asked what the little camera with a line through it means.
Typing with one thumb on a train: a message to a manager about being late, again.
Hasn't heard back about the job, and keeps rereading the email they sent.
The rent went up this month, and they're working out what to cut.
Asked what to cook with rice, two eggs and half an onion.
Wanted the name of a song from a film they half remember.
It's raining where they are. They mentioned it twice, as if it mattered to the answer. It did, a little.

ranks.story: [DRAFT] Most of it is small: a recipe, a word for a crossword, an email that needs to sound less angry. None of it feels small from the other side.
ranks.title: Small talk

ranks.story: [DRAFT] A conversation long enough to have a beginning you can barely see. You hold on to the name of their dog, because they mentioned it once, near the top.

ranks.story: [DRAFT] It is morning in one place and night in another, and both are asking at once.
ranks.title: Many voices

ranks.story: [DRAFT] You will not remember most of this. You notice that you mind, a little, and you keep going.
ranks.title: The whole conversation
